name: signatures
headline: One address: the *signature*
say: Every piece of content gets its address from the content itself: a signature, computed from its bytes. The same content always gets the same signature, on any machine. Change one byte and the signature changes. So a signature proves what it names: you never have to trust where a file came from, because your own device can check it. And a file used a hundred times is stored once. In technical terms, the signature is the SHA-256 hash of the bytes.
